Chooz A (shut down 1991) is drawn for campus context only; the Double Chooz and NUCLEUS baselines refer to B1/B2.

Source conflicts: B1-B2 separation 140 m (TDR 2006 map caption), 160 m (NUCLEUS 2019), 165 m (Double Chooz 2021), 163.3 m (OSM centroids). Far baselines 1114.6/997.9 m (TDR) vs 1115/998 m (2021); near-lab baselines 290.7/260.3 m (TDR preliminary) vs 469/355 m (2021).

The two derived positions rest on building centroids, not reactor axes, and the far-lab construction is ill-conditioned (163 m between circle centres for ~1 km radii); see the geometry records' method text.

summary.plain: The Chooz nuclear power plant's reactor buildings (the old Chooz A unit and the two Chooz B units), the computed positions of the Double Chooz far laboratory in the hill and of the NUCLEUS very-near-site room between the two Chooz B units. The Double Chooz near laboratory is not located.
summary.technical: OSM reactor-unit footprints; far laboratory and NUCLEUS VNS as derived points (two-circle intersections from published baselines with the side fixed by terrain, a neutrino-rate ratio and an OSM building); near laboratory unlocated.

unlocated.backlog: A Double Chooz near-detector civil-engineering plan or paper figure with a scale, the EDF CNPE de Chooz site plan that the NUCLEUS paper credits for its Fig. 2 (which marks the near and far sites), or an OSM/IGN feature for the near-lab shaft building.
unlocated.reason: The near laboratory (~400 m from the cores; 469 m and 355 m to the two cores per arXiv:2009.05515, 120 m.w.e.) has two mirror solutions for each of the two ways the two distances could be paired with B1/B2, and none of the four is selected by a fetched source: the terrain test that settles the far laboratory does not separate them (IGN ground elevations at the four candidates are 114.8 and 105.7 m on the west side of the plant and 132.2 and 107.9 m on the east side, against a plant ground level of 114.7 m, so none sits under a clear hill), and the near-site design figures differ between the TDR (a ~40-45 m deep shaft, 'an overburden of 30 meters of rock') and later papers (about 120 m.w.e., ~400 m from the cores).
